summary: The photo view uses a real optimizer on 2,400 flat Gaussians, with checked compositing and loss derivatives. It is a single-image 2D fit, not a multi-view 3D reconstruction. The one-splat motion is prepared, and the sorting view has a reproducible distance-versus-depth error.

claims.claim: A photo is fit using 2,400 optimized Gaussians.
claims.how: The production fit count is 2,400. Independent pixel compositing agrees with the loss; finite differences agree with all 18 tested derivatives, and a small fit reduces its loss.

sources.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
sources.publisher: Kerbl, Kopanas, Leimkühler, and Drettakis, Inria
sources.says: The method optimizes 3D Gaussian parameters from multiple views, adapts the density of Gaussians, and renders them with visibility-aware splatting.

sources.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
sources.says: Adam uses adaptive estimates of first and second moments of gradients.

claims.claim: The training picture is a single-image 2D version of Gaussian fitting.
claims.how: It optimizes position, two sizes, angle, color, and opacity in a flat photo plane, using Adam and cached frames; it does not optimize full 3D covariance from multiple views.

claims.claim: The one-splat view illustrates optimization with a prescribed path.
claims.how: A shared factor (1−rate) to the step count reduces every target-parameter error for 24 steps, then forces zero. There is no rendered-image loss calculation in this view.

sources.title: Gradient descent
sources.says: Gradient descent moves against the gradient with a chosen step size; its convergence depends on the objective and step size.

claims.note: This resembles gradient descent on a chosen quadratic parameter error; it is not another photometric fit.

claims.claim: The sorting view shows the renderer’s back-to-front order.
claims.how: The bead order is sorted by Euclidean distance to a fixed camera rather than view-axis depth. The test finds pairs whose order disagrees with depth.

sources.title: Gaussian rasterizer depth
sources.says: The renderer uses the Gaussian center transformed into view coordinates and stores its z coordinate as depth.

claims.note: Distance order is not generally the transparency depth order for points away from the center of the view.

simplified: The photo fit uses a reduced-resolution image and 2D parameters, caches its optimization, and replays keyframes. It does not infer a 3D scene from several cameras or adapt the splat count. The one-splat path follows prescribed parameter-error decay and snaps to the target at the end.
